▸ 📰 News Radar · Carson Steele, Tim Patrick, Corey Kiner
Free agents whose role just changed in ESPN's news (last 8 days) -- the breakouts stats can't see yet. Read the blurb, then decide; this ranks, it doesn't predict.
Carson Steele RB✍🌱
PHI · 0.3% owned · 1 GP, 0.0/g · ESPN proj 5.3 (+5.3 vs his pace) · free agent
7d ago · The Eagles signed Steele off the practice squad to the active roster Friday.
Saquon Barkley (hamstring) is considered week-to-week and Tank Bigsby (abdomen) is on injured reserve, so the Eagles added depth to their backfield by signing Steele to the 53-man roster.
Tim Patrick WR✍🌱
NYJ · 0.1% owned · 1 GP, 3.6/g · ESPN proj 5.7 · free agent
6d ago · The Jets activated Patrick (groin) from injured reserve Saturday.
Patrick also doesn't carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Browns, suggesting he's 100 percent healthy.
Corey Kiner RB🆙
NE · 0.8% owned · 5 GP, 1.8/g · ESPN proj 0.0 · free agent
4d ago · Kiner is expected to move into the No. 2 spot on the depth chart behind lead back Rhamondre Stevenson in Sunday's game against the Jets with TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) expected to be sidelined for multiple weeks, Mike Reiss of ESPN.com reports.
After Henderson exited in the second quarter of Sunday's 45-17 win over the Raiders with what was later revealed to be a high-ankle sprain, Kiner stepped in as the top complement to Stevenson and finished the game with six carries for 52 yards, a seven-yard reception and a lost fumble across 15 offensive snaps.

▸ 📖 How to read this · what every number and chip means
Card stripes — The colored bar on each section's left edge says what kind it is: do this · waivers · trades · standings · players · reference
Score 82 50 30 — One 0–100 number per player at every position (IDP and K included), same scale everywhere: 50 = the median starter at his position, 80 = top 10%. Built ~60% from usage (snaps, target/carry/red-zone share, expected points), ~25% from fantasy points in this league's scoring, and the rest from efficiency (EPA, separation, yards over expected). Usage leads because it's the most stable week to week and predicts next week best. IDP: snap share, tackles, sacks + QB hits, pass breakups and fantasy points in TKE's own scoring. K: fantasy points + kick volume.
Early season — Every stat is blended with his 2025 line, and that blend fades fast: after 3 games this season his current usage is ~60% of the number, after 6 it's ~75%. If he changed teams, last season counts half as much. Rookies are pulled toward the position median instead.
U / P / E — Usage, production and efficiency as percentiles at his position. High U + low P is the classic buy: the role is there and the points usually follow.
Form 🔥91↑70↓44❄30 — His last 2 games scored on the same scale, compared with his season score: 🔥 hot (12+ higher), ↑ warm (5+), ↓ cool, ❄ cold. Same cutoffs as the baseball digest. Only shown for players with a real role.
Role ⤴18⤵15 — Snap share in his last game vs his earlier games, in percentage points. Moves before the points do.
PPG / xFP — Actual fantasy points per game vs what his usage should produce (nflverse's expected-points model). Amber = scoring above his usage (TD luck, likely to cool); green = below it (likely to rise).
Edges ▲ run D▼ pressure — This week's opponent, only when they're top-8 or bottom-8 of 32. Receivers are matched by where they catch the ball: a deep threat (average target 12+ yards downfield) is judged against the defense's deep-pass EPA allowed, an underneath receiver against short passes. That's a stand-in for WR-vs-cornerback matchups, since true shadow-coverage data isn't free. Fast/slow game = both offenses' pace between neutral snaps.
Pass vs exp — How much more (or less) a team throws than a typical team would in the same down, distance, score and time (neutral situations only, so garbage time doesn't skew it). The cleanest read on play-caller intent.
Built 2026-10-17 20:41 UTC from ESPN + nflverse (play-by-play, snap counts, FTN charting, Next Gen Stats).
